# Configuration

Every setting, its environment variable, default and meaning — generated from `remote_desktop/config.py` (issue #23). Secrets are redacted. Validate a deployment with `python3 control.py --check-config`.

<!-- Generated by `python3 control.py --gen-config-docs` — do not edit by hand. -->

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `RD_USER` | str | `admin` | Login username shown on the login page. |
| `RD_PASSFILE` | path | `(redacted)` | File holding the crypt SHA-512 password hash (create with: `openssl passwd -6`). Contents are never logged. |
| `RD_FILES_DIR` | path | `~/Downloads` | Directory for file upload/download (created if missing). Used as the default (single) shared root. |
| `RD_FILES_ROOTS` | str | `` | Shared roots for the file manager (#84): comma-separated PATH[:LABEL[:FLAGS]] with FLAGS "ro" and/or "quota=BYTES". Empty = single root from RD_FILES_DIR. Example: "/data/projects:Projects:ro,/srv/media:Media:quota=1073741824". |
| `RD_FILES_RESERVE` | bytes | `67108864` | Free-space reserve per root (#89): uploads that would leave less free space are refused (0 disables). |
| `RD_TRUSTED_PROXIES` | csv | `` | Comma-separated proxy IPs allowed to set X-Forwarded-For. |
| `RD_BIND` | str | `127.0.0.1` | Address the control server binds. Keep the default and put an HTTPS proxy in front for remote access. |
| `RD_PORT` | port | `8090` | TCP port for the single control server (HTTP + websocket + audio). |
| `RD_DISPLAY` | str | `:1` | X display used by xdotool/xclip/xrandr child processes. |
| `VNC_HOST` | str | `127.0.0.1` | Host of the VNC server the websocket proxy connects to. |
| `VNC_PORT` | port | `5901` | Port of the VNC server (Xvnc :1 by default). |
| `RD_GEOMETRY` | geometry | `1280x800` | Desktop size WIDTHxHEIGHT used by session.sh when starting Xvnc. |
| `RD_DPI` | dpi | `96` | Font DPI for the desktop session (session.sh / xrandr --dpi). |
| `REMOTE_CAM_DEVICE` | str | `` | Webcam device for cam-in (default: first /dev/video*). |
| `RD_LOG_FILE` | path | `/tmp/remote-control.log` | Structured log sink (rotated). |
| `RD_LOG_LEVEL` | level | `INFO` | Minimum log level: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING or ERROR. |
| `RD_LOG_FORMAT` | format | `text` | Log record style: text or json. |
| `RD_MAX_CONNECTIONS` | int | `64` | Maximum concurrent TCP connections served (hard bound on threads). |
| `RD_MAX_WS` | int | `32` | Maximum concurrent /websockify VNC websocket proxies. |
| `RD_MAX_AUDIO` | int | `8` | Maximum concurrent audio streams (ffmpeg children). |
| `RD_MAX_MEDIA_IN` | int | `2` | Maximum concurrent device-in streams (mic + webcam). |
| `RD_HTTP_TIMEOUT` | duration | `120` | Seconds an idle keep-alive HTTP connection is kept open. |
| `RD_WS_IDLE_TIMEOUT` | duration | `300` | Seconds a websocket may stay silent before it is closed. |
| `RD_WS_SEND_TIMEOUT` | duration | `5` | Seconds to wait for a websocket client to accept bytes before it is dropped as slow. |
| `RD_WS_MAX_MESSAGE` | bytes | `8388608` | Cap on any single websocket message from the client. |
| `RD_WS_HIGH_WATER` | bytes | `4194304` | Buffered-bytes high-water mark per websocket direction; a peer exceeding it is disconnected. |
| `RD_VNC_RETRIES` | int | `5` | Reconnect attempts to the VNC server before a proxy gives up. |
| `RD_VNC_BACKOFF` | float | `0.5` | Initial reconnect backoff in seconds (doubles, capped at 4s). |
| `RD_STATE_DIR` | path | `~/.local/share/remote-desktop` | Directory for backups, display state and the state manifest. |
| `RD_ARCHIVE_CAP` | bytes | `2147483648` | Maximum uncompressed size when creating or extracting an archive (#85). |
| `RD_TRANSFER_RETENTION` | duration | `86400` | Seconds completed/failed transfer-queue jobs are kept before GC (#88). |
| `RD_READY_CACHE` | duration | `2` | Seconds readiness probes (/api/ready) results are cached. |
| `RD_CONFIG` | path | `(empty)` | Optional KEY=VALUE config file; real environment variables override it (precedence: defaults < file < environment). |

Precedence: schema defaults < `RD_CONFIG` KEY=VALUE file < real environment variables.
